active.title: [Bug] 更新最新版本后“自动跟随系统代理”失效，导致上游请求 502 超时

new.body:
Adding a related case before `fix/1139-issue-1139` lands:

The proposed fix exempts domains resolving to **loopback** (`127.x`), which is great, but the same `onLAN` auto-bypass also breaks **RFC1918 private-IP** endpoints (e.g. `10.x.x.x` / `172.16.x.x` internal gateways) that are **only reachable through the user's system/VPN HTTP proxy** (not directly on the local LAN).

Because `onLAN` is applied automatically and cannot be opted out via standard `NO_PROXY` (which only means "bypass proxy", not "force proxy"), users currently have to configure a per-provider proxy override as a workaround. An opt-out toggle for automatic LAN proxy bypass (or per-provider/global force-proxy rule) would cleanly cover both loopback and RFC1918-over-proxy environments.

repository.name: magpie

issue.body:
### magpie version

0.1.4834

### Where

CLI + gateway (`http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1`)

### OS

macOS 27.2.0 (darwin/arm64)

### Agent, provider and model

plugin `opencode-antigravity-auth` 2.1.2 (npm `dist-tags.latest`), plugin provider id **google** → shown as `google-plugin` (Google, 25 models) → any Gemini model

### Steps to reproduce

1. `magpie plugin add opencode-antigravity-auth`
2. `magpie plugin login google` → `1. OAuth with Google (Antigravity)` → signed in as a personal Gmail account (`✓ signed in to Google · its models are google-plugin/<model>`)
3. Pick any id from the catalog magpie shows (`magpie models`, `24 exposed of 25 · fetched just now`), e.g. `google-plugin/gemini-4-hydrogen`:

```console
$ curl http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer magpie' \
    -d '{"model":"google-plugin/gemini-4-hydrogen","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say ok"}]}'
```

### What happened, and what you expected

**What happened:** every catalog id answers HTTP 404, `Requested entity was not found`:

```text
Google: Requested entity was not found.

[Debug Info]
Requested Model: gemini-4-hydrogen
Effective Model: gemini-4-hydrogen
Project: aicode-consumers
Endpoint: https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse
Status: 404
```

404 on the same account/provider for every id I tried from the list:
`gemini-4-hydrogen`, `gemini-4-neon`, `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-pro-latest`,
`gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.6-flash`,
`claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-5-thinking`, `claude-sonnet-4-5-thinking`.

The same account, same provider, same gateway — **effort-suffixed ids work**:

| model | result |
|---|---|
| `google-plugin/gemini-4-hydrogen-low` | 200 `ok` |
| `google-plugin/gemini-4-hydrogen-medium` | 200 `ok`, 1.45s |
| `google-plugin/gemini-4-hydrogen-high` | 200 `ok`, 2.21s |
| `google-plugin/gemini-3.8-flash-medium` | 200 `ok` |
| `google-plugin/gemini-3.8-flash-high` | 200 `ok`, 4.62s |
| `google-plugin/gemini-3-pro-high` / `-low` | 200, body says “Gemini 3 Pro is no longer available. Please switch to Gemini 3.1 Pro…” |
| `google-plugin/gemini-4-argon-*`, `-carbon-*`, `-neon-*`, `gemini-3.1-pro-*`, `gemini-3.6-flash-*` | 404 |

So the catalog magpie shows and the account's real entitlement are two different id sets, and the visible one is 100% dead — a user cannot discover `-low/-medium/-high` on their own.

The catalog is not coming from the plugin's static list: `.dist` of `opencode-antigravity-auth@2.1.2` contains no `gemini-4-neon` / `gemini-4-hydrogen`, while magpie's list also carries side models such as `lyria-3-*`, `gemini-3-pro-image` (Nano Banana Pro), `deep-research-*-04-2026` — i.e. it looks like the models.dev Google catalog, not what `v1internal` serves for this account.

**What I expected:** the exposed list matches the account's entitlement (including the effort variants), or unknown ids are probed and dropped, so that picking a model from the list works.

Related, possibly the same root cause from other angles: #6704 (built-in antigravity provider: fetched list has no `gemini-4-*`, picking by display name 404s), #5268 (`Gemini Pro models answer 404 on daily-cloudcode-pa`), #3027 / #3617 / #5679 (`gemini-4-argon` 404).

issue.body:
最近在 Windows 上用 Pi 连接同机运行的 Magpie（`127.0.0.1:3425`）时，第一条模型请求就报了 `UND_ERR_SOCKET`，加上 3 次重试全都失败了。翻了下 Clash 日志，发现这四次发往 `127.0.0.1:3425` 的连接都命中了 `MATCH`，被转发到了非 `DIRECT` 出口。

把 `IP-CIDR,127.0.0.1/32,DIRECT,no-resolve` 加到 Clash 规则前面后再测：首次请求、立刻复用连接、空闲 31 秒后再请求，三次都收到了完整的 SSE 响应。Clash 日志也确认新连接命中了 `127.0.0.1/32 → DIRECT`。

建议在 Troubleshooting 里补充一条排查项：当客户端和 Magpie 位于同一主机且使用回环地址时，可以查一下代理日志，确认实际网关地址命中的规则和出口。文档里可以用上面的 Clash 规则作示例，顺带提一句：支持 `NO_PROXY` 的客户端也可以按实际目标地址配置绕过。对于 WSL、容器或远程网关，不要直接照抄 `127.0.0.1`。

相关讨论：#3137

issue.title: gateway: the whole-number rewrite changes numbers inside a custom tool's input

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### magpie version

v0.1.4599. The same code is on `main` at `01e4d9d` (v0.1.4843).

### Where

Gateway only

### OS

Linux arm64, Docker

### Agent, provider and model

Codex (Responses) with a custom tool (`exec` in code mode, `apply_patch`) → a provider magpie translates for, which is offered the tool as a function with one `input` string

### Steps to reproduce

Have the model write the custom tool's arguments with quotes inside `input` that it did not escape, for example:

```
{"input":"x = "2.0"; v = "1.0.2"; n = 3.0"}
```

### What happened, and what you expected

**What happened.** `wholeEncoder` (`internal/gateway/grok_integral.go`) wraps every encoder and runs each call's arguments through `wholeNums`. `wholeNums` tells strings by their unescaped quotes. Between two of these quotes inside `input` it takes the text for JSON outside a string, so it drops the zero fractions there. Read the way #7753 proposes, the tool then receives `x = "2"; v = "1.2"; n = 3.0`. The code runs, with other values. With one unescaped quote, a `1.0` after it becomes `1` as well. With escaped quotes nothing changes. A reply that is not streamed goes the same way, through `wholeResult`.

Today, without #7753, such a call's input is the raw arguments and is broken anyway. Once the input is read as the model meant it, these changed numbers are what runs.

**What I expected.** A custom tool's arguments carry free-form input (code, a patch) in one string. They are not numbers a client parses as integers, so `wholeEncoder` and `wholeResult` should leave a call to a custom tool as it came. Function calls keep the rewrite from #1431 and #3152.

### A fix

This repository takes pull requests from collaborators only, so the change is on a branch: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...saiswj:magpie:chat-tool-call-fixes (two commits on `88222ca`). The second, `90aad12`, is this fix. `wholeEncoder` stops rewriting a call's arguments once `KToolStart` names a custom tool of the request (`Namespaced[name].Custom`), and `wholeResult` skips such calls, so a call to a custom tool is left as it came. Function calls keep the rewrite. The first commit is a separate issue about the chat decoder.

New tests: `TestCustomToolCallKeepsItsNumbers` (unescaped quotes inside `input`, one unescaped quote, escaped quotes, and a function call beside them whose `2500.0` still becomes `2500`) and `TestWholeResultLeavesCustomToolsAsTheyCame`. On the branch, `go test -tags nogui -run '^(TestChatRepeatedToolHeader|TestCustomToolCallKeepsItsNumbers|TestWholeResult|TestRepeatedToolCallIDKeepsParallelCalls|TestInterleavedToolCalls|TestWholeNums|Test[A-Za-z]*(Give|Get)CodexIntegers|Test[A-Za-z]*GiveIntegersOnEveryProtocol|TestToolSearchWholeFloatLimitGivesCodexIntegers|TestStitchedCRAndWholeFloatsBothGo|TestCustomInput|TestCustomTool|TestCodexCustomTool|TestCallArgsStream|TestResponsesCallArgsStream|TestChat[A-Za-z0-9_]*Tool)' ./internal/gateway/` passes: 321 tests and subtests, and `TestGrokPluginCallsGiveCodexIntegers` skipped because there was no bun on PATH.

issue.title: Gateway: Hermes streaming fails on Raccoon SenseNova Flash when assistant history carries both reasoning fields

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### magpie version

Reproduced on a fork based on upstream `v0.1.4717` (fork version `0.1.4717-p1`).

### Where

Gateway only, on Linux (Docker).

### Agent, provider and model

Hermes Agent using a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a LAN → Magpie Chat relay → Raccoon (商汤小浣熊) → `sn-sensenova-6-8-flash-p`.

### Steps to reproduce

Hermes can replay the same assistant reasoning under both `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` for a LAN custom endpoint. To reproduce without Hermes, send the following synthetic body to Magpie's `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a configured Raccoon account. Pin the model so each run reaches the same member.

```json
{
  "model": "raccoon/sn-sensenova-6-8-flash-p",
  "stream": true,
  "reasoning_effort": "max",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "Use the supplied result and reply briefly."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the number?"},
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "",
      "reasoning": "I will look up the number.",
      "reasoning_content": "I will look up the number.",
      "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_example1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_number", "arguments": "{}"}}]
    },
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_example1", "content": "2"}
  ],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_number", "description": "Return the number two.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}}}]
}
```

Repeat with only `reasoning_content` on the assistant message, then with only `reasoning`. Keep the model, messages, tool and streaming settings otherwise identical.

### What happened, and what you expected

| Assistant reasoning fields | Observed on the pinned model |
| --- | --- |
| Both, with equal text | The provider returned `inference request is invalid` on two runs. |
| Only `reasoning_content` | Nonempty assistant text and a completed stream. |
| Only `reasoning` | Nonempty assistant text and a completed stream. |

In the original incident Hermes received the upstream error as an SSE error event, stopped after three attempts. Expected a completed stream with the assistant's reasoning and tool history preserved. A shorter streaming request also reproduced the failure without tools or an effort setting. A short non-streaming control with both fields returned text.

In this case both fields are already present in the incoming request. [#3165](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3165) covers the related case where the gateway added a second field while preparing a tool turn.

### Error text

```text
inference request is invalid
```

issue.title: [Bug] Command Code 的 Anthropic 端点拒绝 tool_result 里的 tool_reference：400 "Invalid input at messages.N.content"，ToolSearch 之后整个会话不可用

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
## 环境

- magpie 0.1.4823；上游 main `df26923a1` 同样存在
- Provider：Command Code（keyed preset，Anthropic base `https://api.commandcode.ai/provider`）
- 模型：`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- 客户端：Claude Code 2.1.332，ToolSearch 可用

## 现象

Claude Code 调用一次 ToolSearch 加载工具后，下一次请求开始每次 400：

```
Command Code: Invalid input at messages.72.content
```

同一会话连续 8 次全部失败（15:48 4 次、15:56 4 次），只有换 provider 或新建会话才能继续。`messages.72` 就是 ToolSearch 的 `tool_result`（magpie 已把 messages 里的 system 消息移到顶层，下标比客户端原数组少一）。

## 最小复现

经 magpie 向 `/v1/messages` 发送（直连 Command Code 的 `/provider/v1/messages` 结果相同）：

```json
{
  "model": "commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "max_tokens": 32,
  "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
  "tools": [
    {"name": "ToolSearch", "description": "Find a tool.", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query"]}},
    {"name": "TaskStop", "description": "Stop a task.", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}
  ],
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "stop the background task"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "Loading TaskStop."},
      {"type": "tool_use", "id": "call_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"query": "select:TaskStop"}}
    ]},
    {"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1", "content": [
        {"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "TaskStop"}
      ]}
    ]}
  ]
}
```

结果（2026-11-26 直连真实端点验证）：

- `content` 只有 `tool_reference` → `400 Invalid input at messages.2.content`
- 在 references 前加一个 `text` block → 仍然 `400 messages.2.content`（不是“只有 references 才不行”，是 `tool_reference` 本身）
- 把 `content` 换成纯文本（字符串，或只有一个 `text` block）→ `200`

所以 Command Code 的 Anthropic 端点不接受 `tool_result` 里的 `tool_reference`，而 Claude Code 的 ToolSearch 答案正是它。

## 根因

`internal/gateway/anthropic_shapes.go` 的 `refuseShapes` 只有两种方式学会把这个 block 换成文本：

- `refsRefused`：错误正文里点名 `tool_reference`（例如 `... got 'tool_reference'`）
- `refsOnlyRefused`：OpenDesign 的 `missing field `content``

Command Code 的 400 只给消息下标，不提 block 类型，所以 magpie 不标记 `shapeRefs`，把 400 原样返回；客户端重试时历史没变，每次都是同一个 400。

## 建议修复

在 `refuseShapes` 里读取 `Invalid input at messages\.(\d+)\.content` 的下标，在“实际发送的 body”里看该消息的 content：若其中有 `tool_result` 且它的 content 含 `tool_reference`，就标记 `shapeRefs`；下一次尝试走现有的 `withRefsAsText`，把 references 换成 `Tool <name> is loaded and can be called now.`，并把对应工具去掉 `defer_loading`。若该消息不含 reference，则保持原样返回，避免吞掉真正的 content 错误。

核心改动：

```diff
@@ var (
 	refsExpected = lazyre.New("(?i)expected [`'\"\\\\]*tool_reference\\b")
+	contentRefused = lazyre.New(`Invalid input at messages\.(\d+)\.content\b`)
 )
...
@@ func (s *Server) refuseShapes(...)
+	if m := contentRefused.FindSubmatch(errBody); m != nil {
+		sent := s.withoutRefusedShapes(p, body)
+		holds := false
+		getIn(sent, "messages."+string(m[1])+".content").ForEach(func(_, b gjson.Result) bool {
+			holds = b.Get("type").String() == "tool_result" && holdsRef(b.Get("content"))
+			return !holds
+		})
+		if holds {
+			mark(shapeRefs)
+		}
+	}
```

## 验证

- 新增 `TestCommandCodeRefsRefusedByContentIndexGoAsText`：旧代码第一次请求直接 400（测试失败）；新代码同一个请求先 400、重试 200，第二次 body 里没有 `tool_reference`、多了文本；再发一次直接从文本开始，不再被拒；另一个接受 references 的 provider 仍原样收到 reference。
- 新增 `TestContentRefusalWithoutARefIsPassedOn`：同样文案但被拒消息不含 reference，原样 400，且只请求一次。
- 直连真实 `api.commandcode.ai/provider`（`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`）：纯 `text` block 的 tool_result 返回 200；`tool_reference`（单独或带 text）返回 400。
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway`（本机 macOS）：72 个 Claude bridge 测试红；其中 `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged` 在未打补丁的 `df26923a1` 上同样红（#3280，`/bin/sh` 为 bash 时 harness 的 echo 问题），其余属于同一 harness（#6766）。本改动相关测试全部通过。
- `go vet`、`GOOS=linux/windows go vet`、三种 `go build` 均通过。

补丁在本地分支 `fix/commandcode-tool-reference-content`（commit `ace738b36`），需要的话我可以贴完整 diff；据仓库说明不接收外部 PR，所以只在这里报告。

@XYenon 谢谢重新评估，逐条说：

1. Pi 1.6.0 给 google-generative-ai 加自定义 fetch 已确认，说明透传签名请求是 Pi 愿意走的方向；但 Chat 协议本身没有签名字段，chat encoder 的 `event()` 也只处理 KStart/KText/KThink/KToolStart/KToolArgs/KError，把 `KTextSig` 这类带过去需要网关侧维护会话状态，不是一次转换能解决的。
2. Opaque Envelope 你也说了不要求，同意不做。
3. xhigh：variant 模型目前已透传（`codeassist.go` 对 variant 直接传 xhigh）；非 variant 模型的"支持 xhigh 却被降级"还缺具体模型证据（你没有指名是哪个），这条先不动，有具体模型名我再核。
4. Raft 共享 models.json：同意这是真阻碍，但网关模型清单如何跨实例共享还没有裁定，不在 fork 里自行设计。

结论：四点没有一条能在不引入会话状态或新共享机制的情况下单独修好，本轮 fork 不动手；维持上游方向（Pi 自带 fetch / OAuth-only），等具体证据或上游裁定。

issue.title: [Bug] Codex PNG inputs fail with IDAT CRC mismatches through Magpie 0.1.4839; identical direct requests succeed

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### What happened

Codex Desktop returned HTTP 400 with a PNG `IDAT` CRC mismatch on a text-only follow-up in a chat with earlier screenshots. I reproduced the same error outside the desktop app with a fresh request containing only synthetic images. The exact same request body succeeded twice when sent directly to the ChatGPT Codex backend and failed twice when sent through the local Magpie gateway.

### Environment

- Magpie 0.1.4839, macOS 14.8.1, arm64
- Codex, ChatGPT sign-in, native OpenAI model `gpt-6.2-astra`, low reasoning effort
- Original surface: Codex Desktop. Controlled reproduction: HTTP POST to the gateway.
- Both routes used the same account and the same outbound HTTP proxy. “Direct” below means bypassing Magpie.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate the synthetic Responses API request below. I used Python 3 and Pillow 12.1.0 on macOS. It contains three valid PNGs, each with a four-digit number on a white label.
2. Using your own ChatGPT Codex authorization, POST the saved JSON bytes once to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` and once to the local Magpie gateway at `/backend-api/codex/responses`. Use identical request bodies and client headers, including `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: text/event-stream`.
3. Repeat with the same file. In this test the temporary Magpie gateway was started fresh for each pair.

<details><summary>Generate the request locally (no credentials needed)</summary>

```python
import base64
import hashlib
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

content = [{
    "type": "input_text",
    "text": "Read the black four-digit code on each white label in order. Output just the codes in order.",
}]
font = ImageFont.truetype("/System/Library/Fonts/SFNSMono.ttf", 160)
for index, code in enumerate(("7319", "2546", "8372")):
    pixels = random.Random(481 + index).randbytes(1000 * 900 * 3)
    image = Image.frombytes("RGB", (1000, 900), pixels)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    draw.rectangle((100, 280, 900, 600), fill="white")
    draw.text((250, 320), code, font=font, fill="black")
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    image.save(buf, format="PNG")
    raw = buf.getvalue()
    Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw)).verify()
    content.append({
        "type": "input_image",
        "image_url": "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(raw).decode(),
    })

request = {
    "model": "gpt-6.2-astra",
    "reasoning": {"effort": "low"},
    "instructions": "Return just the codes.",
    "input": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
    "store": False,
    "stream": True,
}
body = json.dumps(request, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
Path("png-repro.json").write_bytes(body)
print(len(body), hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest())
```

</details>

### Expected and observed results

Both routes should return the three numbers. The tested request was 7,783,016 bytes, SHA-256 `347dfadc2d69929bd7bb4c429fe0155bcfd027f9d0df45577c2ab77b117152c7`.

| Run | Direct | Via Magpie | Matching IDAT chunk in source PNG 1 (byte offset) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | HTTP 200, 7319 / 2546 / 8372 | HTTP 400, expected `0x478a9b7`, have `0xafaf9d9a` | 983253 |
| 2 | HTTP 200, 7319 / 2546 / 8372 | HTTP 400, expected `0x67c5d3b`, have `0x1e068dde` | 589965 |

First error from the synthetic test:

```text
input_image image_url could not parse image: Format error decoding Png: CRC error: expected 0x478a9b7 have 0xafaf9d9a while decoding ChunkType { type: IDAT, critical: true, private: false, reserved: false, safecopy: false } chunk.
```

The original routing log contained 17 calls with this error across three chats. For 12 calls I could match the expected CRC to a valid IDAT chunk in a locally saved chat image. The two controlled runs above failed on different chunks of the same synthetic PNG. I have not compared the gateway's final outbound image bytes with its input, so the exact stage causing the mismatch is still open.

### Related reports

- #2739 discusses upstream request compression for image-heavy Codex turns.
- #3444 reports a WebSocket message-size close and HTTP 502 for a native Codex model. The observable failure here is HTTP 400 during PNG decoding.

These may help narrow the investigation. A shared root cause has not been established.

issue.title: Usage → Requests: T3 Code calls are counted twice — the gateway row (agent `t3code`) never pairs with its `codex` session-file row

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### Summary

On **Usage → Requests**, every call made by **T3 Code** (which drives `codex app-server`) is listed **twice**: once as the gateway request (`agent: t3code`, served model + cost + TTFT filled) and once as a Codex local-session row (`agent: codex`, `provider: session-unknown`, only the requested model name, with served model / cost / TTFT shown as `—`). Both rows carry the **same `response_id`**, so they are the same physical call.

The client asks for a magpie **routing group**, so the requested name is a group alias the gateway resolves into a real model; the local-session row never sees that resolution and can only repeat the alias.

This is the same symptom as #3674, but the blocker here is not a missing id — both sides have it. The id pairing is gated on **both sides being `codex`** (`internal/usage/codex_identity.go:65`), and a T3 Code request is recorded on the gateway side as `agent: t3code`, so the pair is refused and the local-session row stays in the ledger.

### Environment

- magpie version: **0.1.4762** (`magpie version`), bare daemon: `magpie serve --web=127.0.0.1:3430`, systemd user unit, Linux
- Where: **GUI** — Usage → Requests
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu, x86_64)
- Agent, provider and model: **T3 Code** → `codex app-server` → a magpie routing group → two third-party relays plus one ChatGPT subscription account
- Code pointers below are read at tag **v0.1.4762** (commit `161baac4`); the same gate is still present on `main` at `eab4b00`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Point a Codex-based client whose `User-Agent` / `Originator` is not `codex*` — T3 Code runs `codex app-server` this way — at magpie, and select a routing group as the model.
2. Send a few normal turns.
3. Open Usage → Requests. Each call appears as two rows: one `T3 Code` row with the served model and a cost, and one `Codex` row tagged **Local session** carrying the ChatGPT account, the raw group alias only, and `—` for the served model, cost and TTFT.

### What happened, and what was expected

**Happened:** the page lists the same call twice. The Local session row cannot resolve anything beyond the requested group alias, so the served-model and cost columns stay `—`, while its gateway twin shows the real model and cost a few rows away.

**Expected:** one row per call — the same way a request from an agent recorded as `codex` on the gateway side pairs with its session-file row and the Local session duplicate is dropped (`internal/usage/ledger.go:526` skips `matched` local rows).

### Evidence

Two concrete pairs (times are Asia/Shanghai; the local-session rows carry the same `response_id` as their gateway twin):

| Row | time | agent | model column | provider side | in | cache_read | out | cost | ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gateway | 2026-11-25 20:05:48.385 | `t3code` | served model, resolved | relay A | 837 | 242944 | 267 | 8.116656e-05 | 29104 |
| local session | 2026-11-25 20:06:23.924 | `codex` | group alias, unresolved | `session-unknown` | 837 | 242944 | 267 | 0 | 44563 |
| gateway | 2026-11-25 20:04:54.889 | `t3code` | served model, resolved | relay B | 261523 | 0 | 99 | 0.03928785 | 84086 |
| local session | 2026-11-25 20:06:24.946 | `codex` | group alias, unresolved | `session-unknown` | 261523 | 0 | 99 | 0 | 95371 |

`response_id`s are identical inside each pair (both sides of pair 1 end `…b7244`, both sides of pair 2 end `…0b547`).

Scale in this instance, window **2026-11-25 00:05:37 → 20:53:42 (+08)**, 30,000 rows of `GET /api/usage/requests?period=30d&tz=Asia/Shanghai&limit=500&offset=N`:

- **4,229** duplicate pairs, every one of them `(agent: codex, source: log)` + `(agent: t3code, source: null)`. No duplicate pair involves a gateway row recorded as `codex`.
- Local-session side of those pairs: input **36,657,402**, cache_read **602,773,248**, output **3,369,086** tokens.
- Gateway side in the same window: input 239,995,428, cache_read 3,323,084,465, output 22,593,460.
- ⇒ page totals read **+17.9% tokens** and **+12.0% cost** on this instance.
- Of the 4,229 duplicated local-session rows, 3,885 requested an unpriced group alias (they only inflate row count and tokens) and **344 requested an alias that does carry a price**, so those inflate cost as well.
- 23,176 of the 25,232 gateway rows in the window are `agent: t3code`, so this is not a rare edge case on a T3-Code-only instance.

Counting method: page `GET /api/usage/requests` with `limit=500` until the window is covered, then group the rows by `response_id` and keep ids that appear exactly twice with one `source: "log"` row and one gateway row.

### Root cause

- `internal/usage/codex_identity.go:65` — the id pairing accepts a pair only when `records[record].Agent == "codex"` **and** `calls[call].Agent == "codex"`. The gateway record of a T3 Code request has `agent: t3code`, so an id that matches on both sides is still refused.
- `internal/usage/ledger.go:406-409` — `logRecord` does carry `ResponseID` for Codex session files, so unlike #3674 the local row does have the id here.
- `internal/usage/ledger.go:526` — local-session rows that are not in `matched` are appended to the ledger, i.e. the page shows them next to their gateway twin.
- The non-id fallback (same native session, equal token counts, near-equal end) does not rescue these rows either: the two rows' end times differ by ~6 s (gateway end 20:06:18.98 vs local row 20:06:24.95), and the recorded durations differ as well (84,086 ms vs 95,371 ms; 29,104 ms vs 44,563 ms).

### Related

- #3674 — same page, same double counting, reported for `dsh`; there the response id never reaches the ledger. Here the id survives and the agent label is what blocks correlation.

### Note

This report describes the observed behaviour and the code path that produces it; no patch is proposed. Happy to re-measure on a build that changes the pairing rule.

issue.title: routing groups: three waits the budgets do not bound (540 s budget, 429 after 20 s or more, 4 m compaction limit)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
Three waits on one routing group, with Magpie `0.1.4750` to `0.1.4829` on macOS and Codex Desktop as the agent. The group: `routing: order`, `firstToken: 90`, six members on two providers (AI Studio and Gemini Web), each member on three accounts. The group budget is 540 s and a compaction has 4 m. Window 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-26, 14,911 requests on this gateway. Aggregated numbers only.

**1. The 540 s budget does not cut an attempt that is still waiting.** Three requests on 11-25 each stayed on one AI Studio account for 1,203 to 1,291 s before it answered 502, and took 1,383 to 1,472 s in all. In the same requests the other accounts did stop at the 90 s first-token limit (504) or answered at once (429). Expected: an attempt that has sent neither a first token nor an error is cut at the first-token limit, or when the group's budget runs out.

**2. A 429 can still take 20 s or more.** Between 11-19 and 11-26, 106 AI Studio tries came back as `429` after 20 s or more (median 62 s, longest 620 s), while the same gateway answers a cooling account's `429` in under 1 s once every account of the model is marked cooling. On 11-26: 7 tries, 20 to 81 s, three of them inside compaction requests. Expected: when every account of a model is known to be out of quota until a recorded time, the `429` is answered at once and the request is not sent upstream again.

**3. Compaction and the group budget do not match.** Compaction requests walk the group in order, and the 4 m limit runs out before a later member is reached. Seven compaction requests on this group were canceled at 4 m between 11-19 and 11-26, with inputs of 242K to 632K tokens. In all seven the leading accounts used up the limit on `429`s of 11 to 163 s each, a `502` that took 183 s, or accounts with no first token for 90 s. Expected: a compaction gets its own budget, or a `compact` rule is honored before the group's order. A `compact` rule does avoid it here: after adding one that sends compaction to a fast model first, a 331K-token compaction finished in 19 s.

Related: #3788 (the first-content deadline and non-streaming requests).

issue.title: gateway: agy-cli bridge caps a single reply at 300 s, so large single-file writes fail deterministically and agents retry in a loop

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
Version: remote gateway with the update to v0.1.4783 pending (running an earlier build). Route: provider **Antigravity (local agy CLI)**, model `gemini-4-neon`, in a routing group whose only member is that model.

**What happens**

A Claude Desktop session asked a subagent to write a large `app.js` in a single write. Every attempt ended with `200 · api_error`, zero output tokens, and this record on the request:

`agy bridge: timed out reading agy output after 300000ms; stderr tail: (empty)`

Three attempts in the same session:

- 01:24:25 → 462,563 ms
- 02:01:05 → 461,767 ms
- 02:10:38 → 362,288 ms

No usage metadata, no cost. The session itself diagnosed the loop: the Foundation phase wrote `styles.css` (80 KB), `data.js` (61 KB) and `icons.js` (11 KB); the Application phase then tried to emit the whole `app.js` in one call, hit the 5-minute cutoff on every attempt, and each retry re-read the three files — 167 reads, 0 writes.

The same route is healthy for normal turns: over the same day it served ~1.1K requests / 120M tokens at 103–123 tok/s with 3–8 s TTFT. At ~110 tok/s, 300 s of streaming is ~33K output tokens, so any single reply larger than that can never finish through the bridge.

**Why it matters**

For large single-file generations this is deterministic, not a network flake: the reply is cut at 300 s, the record carries an empty stderr, and the agent gets no distinguishable signal, so it retries the same unfinishable attempt (re-reading the prompt each time). A single turn can burn three consecutive 5-minute timeouts.

**Expected**

- A distinct, non-retryable error at the cutoff (e.g. 504 / "agy bridge produced no output for 300 s") so agents can back off or split the write, and fail over immediately instead of waiting.
- A configurable bridge read timeout per provider (I couldn't find one in the provider UI).
- If agy itself caps a generation at 5 minutes, documenting that limit (≈33K output tokens at typical Gemini speed) would help.

**Workaround**

Write large files in chunks / split into modules, keep a single write under ~20–30 KB, or use another provider for turns that emit one very large file.

**Related**

#5043 (long waits then cancel/retry on a Claude subscription) is a similar wait-then-retry shape on another route.

active.title: [Bug] 重置前用完(pace)路由不按"即将到期"排序：CodeArts / OfficeAce 每日签到积分（次日过期）在路由组/多账号里不被优先消耗

issue.title: [Bug] officeace (opencode-codearts-auth): an account whose windows are all spent stays in the routing order at pace 0, and its 401 takes the 1-2-4 failure ladder so quota-rest never applies

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### Environment

- magpie `0.1.4731` (container `magpie:0.1.1564-glibc`)
- `officeace` is served by **`@magpie-community/opencode-codearts-auth@0.3.22`** — the same plugin that serves `codearts` (`magpie plugin` lists both providers under it; `index.mjs` references OfficeAce throughout), so its windows are built there.
- 3 accounts on the same plan; `routing=pace`
- `magpie provider quota-rest officeace "00:00+08:00"` is set and reads back as
  `sits out until 00:00+08:00`

### Symptom

An OfficeAce account whose every window is spent (`总积分` used 100%, 0 left) **stays in the routing `order`** and keeps being selected, so the gateway gets `401` over and over. The card shows `401 · 失败 · 4 分钟后恢复` — the *failure* ladder (1→2→4…, default cap 10m), not the quota rest. Because that ladder is short, the account is retried every few minutes for the rest of the day and fails every time.

`quota-rest until 00:00+08:00` therefore never applies: the response is classified as a plain failure, so the "out of allowance" branch is never entered.

### Evidence

Quota windows of the three accounts:

```
01a17bc3…  总积分 · 剩 44.53   used=87   limit=350   resetsAt=None   runsOut=44.53
01a1c447…  总积分 · 剩 0       used=100  limit=4550  resetsAt=None
0bd51f6a…  总积分 · 剩 0       used=100  limit=4550  resetsAt=None
```

The very next routing record still carries the two spent accounts:

```
"order": [
  { "who": "01a17bc3…", "used": 87,  "amount": 305.47, "pace": 0.0774, "rank": 2 },
  { "who": "0bd51f6a…", "used": 100, "amount": 4550,   "pace": 0,      "rank": null },
  { "who": "01a1c447…", "used": 100, "amount": 4550,   "pace": 0,      "rank": 1 }
]
```

Two things stand out:

1. An account at `pace: 0` (nothing left) is still a candidate rather than held.
2. `01a1c447…` at `pace: 0` even carries `rank: 1`, ahead of the account that actually has 44.53 credits — so once the good account is spent, the spent one is what gets asked next.

Once selected, the gateway gets `401`, which lands on the failure ladder — hence the `4 分钟后恢复` in the card instead of a rest to the daily renewal.

### Why `quota-rest` doesn't rescue it

`limit-notices.json` has no entry for these accounts at all (contrast `trae-cn` and `qwen-cn`, which do get `why:"quota"`), i.e. the `401` was never classified as out-of-allowance. So the `quota-rest until 00:00+08:00` branch is unreachable for OfficeAce.

This looks like the same class as **#5111** (closed: a 429 "Budget has been exceeded" read as a short rate limit, so `quota-rest until HH:MM` never applied) — but for a **401** the gateway still takes the failure path.

### The expiry signal also never reaches `pace`

For this account the routing record carries `renews: ["0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"]` (the `总积分` window has **no** `resetsAt`) and `soon` / `lapse` only ever show `2026-12-20T03:40:47Z`. The daily check-in bucket that expires the next morning (`每日签到有礼`, `resetsAt 2026-11-24T15:59:59Z`) is a separate window, so it is invisible to the pace ranking — the same shape described in **#4923**.

Since `officeace` is built by the codearts plugin, that plugin could stamp the soonest live bucket's `runsOutAt` / `runsOut` on the longest-lived window the way its own `codearts` provider already does for its total window (and the way MYCF711/magpie-officeace#48 does for that plugin). The `codearts` provider ranks correctly here; `officeace` from the same package does not.

Related: **#3428** (the seat knows *when* something lapses but not *how much*), **#6907** (near-cap spillover bypassing "Until used up" while quota remains), **#7618** (`routing=order` + expiry composing via `prefer=expiring`).

### Expected

Either of:

- an account whose non-aside windows are all spent is held until its window renews, **or**
- a `401` that the vendor returns for an exhausted account is classified as out-of-allowance so the provider's `quota-rest` (`until 00:00+08:00` here) applies, instead of the 1→2→4 failure ladder.

And for the pacing half, `officeace`'s windows in `opencode-codearts-auth` should carry the soonest live bucket's `runsOutAt` / `runsOut` on the longest-lived window — otherwise `pace` can never rank OfficeAce by what it is about to lose.

### Repro

1. Two OfficeAce accounts with all windows at 0, one with credits left; `routing=pace`, `quota-rest` at any `HH:MM`.
2. Send requests until the funded account is spent.
3. The two spent accounts come up in `order` (`pace: 0`), get `401`, and rest 1→2→4 minutes rather than until the daily renewal; `limit-notices.json` records nothing for them.

issue.title: [feat] routing: one strategy per level means "in order" and "use before expiry" cannot be combined — ask for a second key (prefer=expiring) that re-orders within the tier instead of replacing the rule

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### What I want

Pick **two** routing behaviours at once for the same level, e.g. "In order" **+** "Use before expiry", meaning:

> go through my models/accounts **in my order**, but among those that are candidates, take the one that is about to expire first — i.e. cycle the accounts by expiry time.

Today a level takes exactly one strategy, so the two are mutually exclusive.

### What exists today (0.1.4731)

There are already **two** levels, and each takes a single value:

- **Routing group** (`magpie group set <id> routing=…`): `smart` (default) · `order` · `drain` · `rotate` · `usage` · `pace` · `weight` · `manual`
  - `magpie group` help: `smart` = *"of the subscriptions with quota to spare, the one renewing soonest first"* — expiry, but it ignores the member order
  - `order` = *"the first model until it can't answer, then the next"* — my order, but it ignores expiry
- **Provider** (`magpie provider set <id> routing=…`): `smart` · `order` · `rotate` · `usage` · `pace` · `weight` · `free` · `fast` · `drain`
  - `pace` = *"the account with the most of its week left per hour until it renews first"* — expiry again, ignoring `accountOrder`
  - `order` = follows `accountOrder`, ignoring expiry

So at every level it is **order XOR expiry**. There is no `order`+expiry.

### Cross-layer composition already works — and it is not enough

Worth recording, because it is the workaround and it shows the machinery is there. A group `order` composes with a provider `pace`:

```
magpie group set auto-deepseek-flash routing=order     # my order across providers
# provider routing stays pace                          # expiry across that provider's accounts
```

Probe (models 1…8 on the group; #1 `trae-cn` is held at its cap, #2 `officeace`):

```
model=group/auto-deepseek-flash
order[0] officeace@01a17bc3…  routing=pace  pace=0.0714   ← #1 trae skipped, held
order[1] officeace            routing=pace  pace=None
order[3] loomy@手动粘贴 ···2e6d74 routing=pace  pace=8.2219
=> served officeace@01a17bc3…
```

That gives "in my order across providers, expiry within each". What it can **not** give is "in my order **and** expiry at the same level" — e.g. on one provider with 4 accounts, or in a flat group where I numbered the models myself and want the soonest-expiring one among the first few to go first.

### Concrete case

Group `auto/deepseek-flash` carries a hand-visible order (1 trae-cn · 2 officeace · 3 scnetplan · 4 loomy · 5 tokenrhythm · 6 codearts · 7 raccoon · 8 intern-inkstone) **and** `routing=pace`. With `pace` the numbered order is decorative — a member at #8 with a high weekly pace is served before #1. With `order` the expiry is decorative — #1 is drained even when #8's credits vanish tomorrow.

I want: keep #1 first **while it has room and is not the one about to lose credits**, then #2, and so on — i.e. order as the tier, expiry as the tie-break inside the tier.

### Suggestion

Something like a second key rather than a new strategy enum, so existing values keep their meaning:

```
magpie group set <id> routing=order prefer=expiring
magpie provider set <id> routing=order prefer=expiring
```

- `routing` stays the primary rule (unchanged semantics, so `TestAllowancePace` / #517 stay pinned);
- `prefer` re-orders **within** whatever tier the primary rule produced (here: within "the first model that can answer", and within an `order` provider's `accountOrder`);
- with `prefer=expiring`, the seat's `Lapse` / `Allowance.RunsOut` is the comparator, which the gateway already carries (the routing log prints `lapse` and `soon` per candidate today).

That avoids the min→max argument in #4923 entirely: `prefer` never changes *which tier* an account is in, only the order inside it, so the "tightest window" pacing semantics are untouched.

### Related

- **#4923** — pace not ranking by what is about to be lost (officeace shape); the triage there settled on folding expiry into `pace`, which is the "expiry" half of this request
- **#3428** — the seat carries *when* an allowance expires but not *how much*, which bounds how good any expiry tie-break can be
- **#6907** — near-cap spillover bypassing "Until used up" while quota remains
- **#7034** — `routing=expiring` has no expiry input for non-subscription providers (the manual-API half of the same complaint)
- **#4535** — `LeastUsed` treats pay-as-you-go keys as Used 0%, another case of one strategy's key not being read by another

### Environment

magpie `0.1.4731`, 12 routing groups (mostly `pace`, one hand-made `order`), providers routed `pace`.

active.title: 新版 Codex 基础提示词经 Magpie 转发后被重复追加

new.body:
关于 62-token 那次，先说明来源：那不是真实 Claude Code 会话的请求，是我本地的一个测试请求。测试脚本发一个很短的 system（`You are a helpful assistant. Reply with exactly OK.`），本地 Magpie middleware `codex-first-line.middleware.js` 在它前面加官方首行，再发给 Magpie。

所以首行要分三层看：

| 层 | system 首行 | 和官方首行比 |
|---|---|---|
| 中间件之后（Magpie 实际收到） | 官方首行原文 | 一致 |
| 客户端原始（中间件之前） | `You are a helpful assistant...` | 不一致，也不是官方首行的变体 |
| 真实 Claude Code（不加中间件） | 没有样本 | 无法确认 |

对应到你的修法：`codexInputStartsWithCodex` 依赖“首行相等”。我的 62-token 请求在中间件之后能命中，所以你的修法对我这边是生效的；但它不能证明真实 Claude Code 请求（不加中间件）的首行也是官方首行。如果真实请求的首行是 Claude Code 自己的 system 首行，你的判断不会命中，官方提示词仍会加一份。我这边没有不加中间件的真实样本，所以对真实 Claude Code 的情况只能回答“无法确认”。

作为背景，同一个短请求在 v0.1.4624 上的数字是：

| 模型 | system 落点 | total_prompt | 其中官方提示词 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 5.6-luna | `instructions` | 62 | 0（首行直通替换） |
| 6.2-astra | `input` | 5,426 | 5,248（缓存） |

你的修法要解决的是 6.2 这 5,248 的重复；我的本地请求因为有中间件，所以能验证它生效，但不能替真实 Claude Code 请求作证。

known.body:
@wuyak 这条路径应该由 #4953 的修复覆盖，也按你的窄修法做了——它不属于 #2906/#1378 那类"不改 Codex 提示词"的场景：客户端把基础提示词自己的副本放进 input（首行即官方首行），再叠加一份官方文本是重复投递，不是改写。

实现：请求 `instructions` 为空时（Lite 形状本来就没有官方文本，不受影响），若 input 第一条 developer 消息的首行等于官方首行，就认定客户端已自带基础提示词，不再追加官方副本；首行不同则仍是客户端自己的提示词，原样保留。判断与 5.6 现有的 `firstLine(own) == firstLine(codex)` 直通同一标准；#4953 原有形状（整文/模板匹配、`model.base_instructions` 标记）不受影响。

- 分支：[fix/4953-translated-first-line](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/4953-translated-first-line)（提交 58f2c396d，基于当前 upstream/main 8d0226d9b）
- 回归测试 `TestCodexBodyTranslatedFirstLineGetsNoSecondCopy`：把该判断手动去掉后失败（`client's copy: 2 base prompts, want 1`），恢复后通过；`TestCodexBodyAsCodexSendsIt`、`TestCodexBodyLiteGetsNoInstructions` 不受影响。整包 `internal/provider` 里两个 Claude 登录测试在干净 upstream/main 上同样红（本机环境，日志已附基线对照），与本次无关。红/绿/基线日志在 fork 的 `docs/upstream-issue-followup-20261119` 分支 `docs/upstream-issues/2026-11-24/evidence/4953/`。

一个确认请求：5.6 上那份 62-token 的客户端 system，首行是官方首行原文，还是客户端自己的变体？如方便请只贴首行前 ~80 个字符即可，不用全文——这能验证"首行相等"这个判断对真实 Claude Code 够不够准。

new.body:
Confirmed on a build carrying `aca455708`, from `fix/5359-plugin-account-header-fields` (base `ed0ab567`).

- In the editor of a plugin-backed account (`cc-bridge`, my setup from the report), Advanced now shows **Reply headers** and **Request headers to pass**.
- Existing values load: the `passHeaders` I had written into `providers.json` by hand show up in the field.
- On a test account, editing both fields in the page and pressing Save persists both arrays (checked via `/api/providers` afterwards), and the dialog closes as usual.
- I didn't click through the custom-provider editor by hand; that path only moved into the same shared helpers.

So no changes on the gateway side were needed, as the diagnosis said, and the reported case is covered. The declarative `passHeaders` default can stay a separate follow-up.

One note for whoever merges: the branch is based on `ed0ab567`, which is behind current main and may need a rebase. I tested the branch's web UI, not a released build.
